basicControls.label: Strength
basicControls.help: How much of the look is applied. 0 % shows your picture unchanged, 100 % the full look.

basicControls.label: Exposure
basicControls.help: Makes the whole picture brighter or darker, in photographic stops.

basicControls.label: Contrast
basicControls.help: Pushes darks darker and lights lighter, or flattens them for a softer picture.

basicControls.label: Warmth
basicControls.help: Shifts colours towards orange (warmer) or blue (cooler), like a white balance setting.

basicControls.label: Tint
basicControls.help: Shifts colours towards magenta or green, to fix colour casts from lamps or shade.

basicControls.label: Saturation
basicControls.help: Makes colours richer, or paler down to black and white at -100 %.

basicControls.label: Fade
basicControls.help: Lifts the blacks to a milky grey, like an old faded print.

basicControls.label: Grain
basicControls.help: How strong the film grain texture is. 0 % turns it off in effect.

basicControls.label: Grain size
basicControls.help: Fine or coarse grain clumps. Larger grain looks like faster, more sensitive film.

basicControls.label: Film size
basicControls.help: Smaller film is enlarged more, so its grain looks bigger in the picture.

basicControls.label: Halation
basicControls.help: A red-orange glow around bright lights, as on film when light bounces back off the base.

basicControls.label: Glow
basicControls.help: A soft white haze around bright areas, like a lens with a little mist on it.

basicControls.label: Vignette
basicControls.help: Darkens the corners to draw the eye to the middle of the picture.

controls.label: Film type
controls.help: Colour negative is soft and forgiving, slide is punchy with dark shadows, black and white drops colour.

controls.label: Film response
controls.help: Turns the film's tone and colour response on or off. Off shows the other effects alone.

controls.label: Film contrast
controls.help: The film's own contrast in the mid-tones, before printing.

controls.label: Colour crosstalk
controls.help: How much the film's colour layers affect each other. More gives denser, more separated colours.

controls.label: Shadow roll-off
controls.help: How gently the shadows fade to black. Higher keeps more detail in the dark areas.

controls.label: Highlight roll-off
controls.help: How gently bright areas reach white. Higher keeps more detail in skies and lamps.

controls.label: Toning
controls.help: Black and white only: tints the picture brown, like a sepia-toned print.

controls.label: Printer colour trims
controls.help: Turns the cyan, magenta, yellow and brightness trims below on or off.

controls.label: Cyan trim
controls.help: Adds cyan to the print, or red when negative, as a darkroom printer would.

controls.label: Magenta trim
controls.help: Adds magenta to the print, or green when negative.

controls.label: Yellow trim
controls.help: Adds yellow to the print, or blue when negative.

controls.label: Print brightness
controls.help: Prints the whole picture lighter or darker, keeping the film's contrast.

controls.label: Print depth
controls.help: How deep the print's blacks go. Lower looks flatter and greyer.

controls.label: Shadow red
controls.help: More or less red in the shadows only.

controls.label: Shadow blue
controls.help: More or less blue in the shadows only.

controls.label: Highlight red
controls.help: More or less red in the bright areas only.

controls.label: Highlight blue
controls.help: More or less blue in the bright areas only.

controls.label: Halation
controls.help: Turns the red-orange glow around bright lights on or off.

controls.label: Starts at brightness
controls.help: How bright a light must be before it glows. Lower makes more of the picture glow.

controls.label: Onset softness
controls.help: How gradually the glow fades in as lights get brighter.

controls.label: Halation size
controls.help: How far the glow spreads from each light, as a share of picture width.

controls.label: Glow
controls.help: Turns the soft haze around bright areas on or off.

controls.label: Glow size
controls.help: How far the haze spreads, as a share of picture width.

controls.label: Grain
controls.help: Turns the film grain on or off.

controls.label: Grain colour sync
controls.help: High makes grain grey and even; low lets each colour have its own grain, which looks more colourful.

controls.label: Frozen grain
controls.help: Video: keeps one grain pattern instead of new grain on each frame, which looks like a still.

controls.label: Finishing
controls.help: Turns contrast, saturation, fade, white level and vignette on or off together.

controls.label: White level
controls.help: Lowers the brightest white to a soft grey.

controls.label: Vignette size
controls.help: How far from the centre the corners start to darken.

controls.label: Video effects
controls.help: Turns flicker and frame wobble on or off. They only move in video.

controls.label: Flicker
controls.help: Brightness that wavers from frame to frame, like old projected film.

controls.label: Frame wobble
controls.help: The picture drifts slightly from frame to frame, like film moving through a camera.

looks.name: Portra 400 style
looks.info: Portra 400 is a fine-grain ISO 400 portrait colour negative; the look gives soft contrast, gentle highlights and natural skin. Tone curves and colour response follow Kodak's published data (characteristic curves, spectral sensitivities); interlayer effects, grain and halation are tuned by eye. Its tuned split tone warms the highlights, so 90 % white shows warm (blue about 13 % below red).

looks.name: Portra 160 style
looks.info: Portra 160 is a very fine-grain ISO 160 portrait colour negative; the look is low in contrast with muted, natural colour. Tone curves and colour response follow Kodak's published data (characteristic curves, spectral sensitivities); interlayer effects, grain and halation are tuned by eye. Its tuned split tone warms the highlights, so 90 % white shows warm (blue about 10 % below red).

looks.name: Ektar 100 style
looks.info: Ektar 100 is an ISO 100 colour negative with very fine grain; the look is crisp and saturated. Tone curves follow Kodak's published data; colour stays tuned by eye because the colour from Kodak's spectral sensitivities shifts sky hue by 30.9° at +2 stops (limit 30°). Grain and halation are tuned by eye.

looks.name: Gold 200 style
looks.info: Gold 200 is an ISO 200 consumer colour negative; the look is warm with punchy everyday colour. An approximation tuned by eye; the colour from Kodak's published spectral sensitivities was tried and left out because it lost too much saturation (chroma 0.544 of the tuned look, limit 0.6).

looks.name: Pro 400H style
looks.info: Pro 400H was a Fujifilm ISO 400 professional colour negative; the look is airy with cool, slightly green-leaning tones. The colour response follows Fujifilm's published spectral sensitivities; tone, interlayer effects, grain and halation are tuned by eye.

looks.name: CineStill 800T style
looks.info: CineStill 800T is Kodak Vision3 500T cinema film sold for stills without its anti-halation layer; the look is tungsten-balanced with red halos round lights. The colour response follows Kodak's published spectral sensitivities; tone, interlayer effects, grain and halation are tuned by eye.

looks.name: Velvia 50 style
looks.info: Velvia 50 is a Fujifilm slide film famous for landscape work; the look is very saturated with deep blacks. The reversal curve follows Fujifilm's published data, viewed through a display adaptation; deep shadows block up as on the real film. The colour response follows Fujifilm's published spectral sensitivities; interlayer effects, grain and halation are tuned by eye.

looks.name: Provia 100F style
looks.info: Provia 100F is a Fujifilm slide film with neutral colour; the look is clean and moderately saturated. The reversal curve follows Fujifilm's published data, viewed through a display adaptation; deep shadows block up as on the real film. The colour response follows Fujifilm's published spectral sensitivities; interlayer effects, grain and halation are tuned by eye.

looks.name: Ektachrome E100 style
looks.info: Ektachrome E100 is Kodak's current slide film; the look is clean with cool-neutral colour and fine grain. The reversal curve follows Kodak's published data (the dataset's Ektachrome 100D curves), viewed through a display adaptation; deep shadows block up as on the real film. The colour response follows Kodak's published spectral sensitivities; interlayer effects, grain and halation are tuned by eye.

looks.name: Kodachrome 64 style
looks.info: Kodachrome 64 was Kodak's classic slide film, discontinued in 2009; the look has warm reds and dense shadows. The reversal curve follows Kodak's published data, viewed through a display adaptation; deep shadows block up as on the real film. Colour stays tuned by eye: the colour from Kodak's spectral sensitivities lost too much saturation (chroma 0.595 of the tuned look, limit 0.6). Grain and halation are tuned by eye.

looks.name: Tri-X 400 style
looks.info: Tri-X 400 is Kodak's classic fast black-and-white film; the look is gritty with strong mid-tone contrast. Tone curves follow Kodak's published data; colour, grain and halation are tuned by eye.

looks.name: Tri-X 400 style, sepia toned
looks.info: Tri-X 400 printed and sepia toned; the look has warm brown tones. An approximation tuned by eye.

looks.name: HP5 Plus style
looks.info: HP5 Plus is Ilford's fast black-and-white film; this look is soft with open shadows and visible grain. An approximation tuned by eye.

looks.name: T-Max 100 style
looks.info: T-Max 100 is Kodak's fine-grain black-and-white film; this look is smooth and clean. An approximation tuned by eye.

looks.name: Delta 3200 style
looks.info: Delta 3200 is Ilford's very fast black-and-white film; this look is dark and very grainy. An approximation tuned by eye.

looks.name: Vision3 500T style + 2383 print style
looks.info: Vision3 500T is Kodak's fast tungsten cinema negative, here printed on 2383; the look is the classic modern movie image. An approximation tuned by eye; Kodak's 2383 print curve is fitted but not used, because it blocks the shadows on ordinary pictures.

looks.name: Vision3 250D style + 2383 print style
looks.info: Vision3 250D is Kodak's daylight cinema negative, printed on 2383; the look is a clean, natural movie image. An approximation tuned by eye; Kodak's 2383 print curve is fitted but not used, because it blocks the shadows on ordinary pictures.

looks.name: Vision3 50D style + 2393 print style
looks.info: Vision3 50D is Kodak's finest-grain daylight cinema negative, printed on Premier 2393; the look is rich and very clean. The negative's colour response follows Kodak's published spectral sensitivities; tone, print, interlayer effects, grain and halation are tuned by eye; the published 2393 print curve is not used because its fit misses the tolerance.

looks.name: Eterna 500 style + 3513 print style
looks.info: Eterna 500 was Fujifilm's fast cinema negative, printed on Eterna-CP 3513; the look is soft and muted. The negative's colour response follows Fujifilm's published spectral sensitivities; tone, print, interlayer effects, grain and halation are tuned by eye; the published 3513 print curve is not used because its fit misses the tolerance.

looks.name: Portra 800 style
looks.info: Portra 800 is Kodak's fastest portrait colour negative; the look is soft and warm with more visible grain. Tone curves and colour response follow Kodak's published data (characteristic curves, spectral sensitivities); interlayer effects, grain and halation are tuned by eye. Its tuned split tone warms the highlights, so 90 % white shows warm (blue about 13 % below red).

looks.name: Ultramax 400 style
looks.info: Ultramax 400 is an ISO 400 consumer colour negative; the look is warm and contrasty with noticeable grain. The colour response follows Kodak's published spectral sensitivities; tone, interlayer effects, grain and halation are tuned by eye.

looks.name: Superia X-TRA 400 style
looks.info: Superia X-TRA 400 is a Fujifilm ISO 400 consumer colour negative; the look has cooler greens and crisp contrast. Tone curves follow Fujifilm's published data; colour stays tuned by eye because the colour from Fujifilm's spectral sensitivities shifts sky hue by 31.8° at +2 stops (limit 30°). Grain and halation are tuned by eye.

looks.name: Fujicolor C200 style
looks.info: Fujicolor C200 is an inexpensive ISO 200 colour negative; the look is clean with slightly cool, light colour. Tone curves and colour response follow Fujifilm's published data (characteristic curves, spectral sensitivities); interlayer effects, grain and halation are tuned by eye.

looks.name: CineStill 50D style
looks.info: CineStill 50D is Kodak Vision3 50D cinema film sold for stills without its anti-halation layer; the look is fine-grained daylight colour with strong halation. The colour response follows Kodak's published spectral sensitivities; tone, interlayer effects, grain and halation are tuned by eye.

looks.name: Double-X 5222 style
looks.info: Double-X 5222 is Kodak's black-and-white cinema negative; the look is classic film-noir grey scale with visible grain. Tone curves follow Kodak's published data; colour, grain and halation are tuned by eye.

looks.name: Vision3 200T style + 2383 print style
looks.info: Vision3 200T is Kodak's medium-speed tungsten cinema negative, printed on 2383; the look is a fine-grained movie image. An approximation tuned by eye; Kodak's 2383 print curve is fitted but not used, because it blocks the shadows on ordinary pictures.

looks.name: Ektachrome 100D style
looks.info: Ektachrome 100D is Kodak's colour reversal cine film, the same emulsion family as Ektachrome E100, used for Super 8, 16 mm and 35 mm; the look is clean with cool-neutral colour and fine grain. The reversal curve uses the same published curves as the Ektachrome E100 look, which the dataset digitised from Kodak's Ektachrome 100D datasheet, viewed through a display adaptation; deep shadows block up as on the real film. The colour response follows Kodak's published spectral sensitivities; interlayer effects, grain and halation are tuned by eye.

looks.name: ORWO NC500 style
looks.info: NC500 is ORWO's ISO 400 colour negative cine film from 2022, descended from Agfa; the look is muted and fairly flat, with green-cyan shadows, warm highlights, strong grain and red-orange halos round lights. An approximation tuned by eye; no published data was used.
